issues.title: Incorrect response-vector input space
issues.failure_explanation: For S_i in R^{m_i by N}, S_iY is undefined when the declared input has Y in R^d; likewise Y-X beta is dimensionally inconsistent for general N not equal to d. The paper's model and every substantive use require an N-vector response.
issues.overall_effect: The literal contracts of both Alg-framework and Alg-SRHT fail on the paper's intended N-by-d regression problems, making their iterates undefined until the response type is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the response declaration in the input lines of both Alg-framework and Alg-SRHT from Y in R^d to Y in R^N. No update rule or affected result needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The model Y=X beta+zeta, the products S_iY, and all residual dimensions uniquely force an N-vector response, and the analysis already uses that type. This is repeated transcriptional mistyping rather than a defective construction or inference.

issues.title: Undefined operand in the Hessian-sketch construction
issues.failure_explanation: No matrix A is defined in the model or algorithm, so the displayed construction does not specify the preconditioner. The design matrix X has the required dimensions and is used in the later construction and proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The first preconditioner definition is undefined, although a later old-source occurrence already disambiguates the intended construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace A by X in the first definition of the Hessian sketch, giving hat H=(hat S X)^T hat S X.
issues.why_classification: No matrix A exists, while the model, dimensions, later definition, algorithm, and proofs uniquely identify X. The correction requires no mathematical argument or change of guarantee.

issues.title: First-stage M-IHS residual uses the unknown parameter
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm receives the current iterate beta_t but not the true parameter beta. With the printed residual, the update is neither implementable nor the Richardson/M-IHS iteration for the sketched normal equations.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed first-stage update contradicts the executable pseudocode, although the latter and the convergence proof already use the intended current-iterate residual.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation (98), replace S_iX beta-S_iY by S_iX beta_t-S_iY.
issues.why_classification: The current-iterate residual is uniquely forced by the executable pseudocode, the normal equations, and the convergence proof. Restoring the omitted iteration subscript is transcriptional and does not repair any inference used elsewhere.

issues.title: Full-scale M-IHS residual uses the unknown parameter
issues.failure_explanation: Using X beta-Y makes the purported iteration depend on the unknown true parameter and removes the current iterate from the gradient term, so the printed update is not an executable solver for the full normal equations.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed second-stage specification is wrong, while the separately stated pseudocode and convergence recurrence use the intended update.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation (99), replace X beta-Y by X beta_t-Y.
issues.why_classification: The pseudocode and full-scale convergence recurrence already use the uniquely intended current iterate. Adding the omitted subscript restores that specification without changing the algorithmic argument or guarantee.

issues.title: Overall OLS-level bound uses a conditional first-stage comparison

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the subsequent discussions are based on the following conditions:

issues.failure_explanation: Thf claims an OLS-level bound under its finite embedding and iteration hypotheses. The proof obtains the displayed OLS term from finalerror, whose comparison of each sketched-estimator error with the OLS error is made in the asymptotic setting of lemma:lemma3 and under the additional variance condition declared in remarkA7. Those conditions are not hypotheses of Thf, so that dependency is unavailable throughout the theorem's stated regime.
issues.overall_effect: The main OLS-level guarantee is not established over all instances admitted by its statement, and the noise-level justification used by the later complexity theorem inherits the gap.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conditional OLS comparison in finalerror and the proof of Thf by a direct recurrence in the exact sketched-estimator errors. If T_i=sum_{j<=i}a_j, s=T-T^dagger, delta_i=E||X(tilde beta_i-beta)||, and delta_*=E||X(hat beta-beta)||, derive E||X(beta_T-beta)|| <= 3^{-T}E||X(beta_0-beta)|| + sum_i(1+3^{-a_i})3^{-(T-T_i)}delta_i + (1+3^{-s})delta_*. For delta_*>0, bound the finite collection delta_i by C delta_* (and handle the noiseless case separately), yielding the original OLS-level limit as s grows. Carry the resulting C-dependent full-scale iteration threshold through cmpxtyAlgSLSE; the asymptotic complexity orders can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The missing asymptotic spectral and variance premises are substantive restrictions, so merely adding them would narrow Thf's stated regime. A same-guarantee resolution is available from the existing stagewise and full-scale contractions, but it requires a contained replacement recurrence and corresponding complexity bookkeeping rather than a short local edit. It avoids global reconstruction and major loss, so the issue is moderate.

issues.title: Malformed inter-subproblem error ratio
issues.failure_explanation: The statement defines r by the radicand m_{i-1}-d/m_i-d, whereas the proof needs r to bound the preceding sketched-estimator error by the current one and explicitly derives sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)). Thus the argument supports a different iteration bound from the one printed.
issues.overall_effect: The stated lower bound for a_i uses the wrong quantity. The later complexity theorem also uses an incompatible reciprocal expression, so its monotonicity and explicit constant require consistent recalculation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define r(i-1,i)=sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)) in lowerBoundai and use that same ratio throughout its proof and cmpxtyAlgSLSE. For m_i=2^{-(K+1-i)}N and d/N tending to gamma, recompute r_i=sqrt((2-2^{K+2-i}gamma)/(1-2^{K+2-i}gamma)); consequently a_2>...>a_K. Replace the old alpha based on 1/sqrt(2) by a valid bound such as alpha_corr=log_3([1+(1+omega)sqrt((2-2^K gamma)/(1-2^K gamma))]/omega), and propagate alpha_corr and any resulting parameter conditions through the first- and second-stage cost bounds.
issues.why_classification: The primary correction is forced by the proof, but the downstream complexity argument genuinely uses the reciprocal and therefore cannot be repaired as a mere transcription. Consistent recalculation reverses the stated monotonicity and changes the explicit aspect-ratio dependence of the complexity constant, although a comparable lower bound and the same O(Nd) iteration-cost order survive by contained algebra. This limited change makes the issue moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Terminal stage factor omitted from the first-stage recursion
issues.failure_explanation: Applying thm:convergence_theorem1 at stage K contributes [1+3^{-a_K}] times the K-th sketched-estimator error. Equation 22 keeps only the leading K-th error term, so its asserted upper bound does not follow from the induction.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of finalerror, and hence the formal chain through Thf, contains an invalid exact inequality. The omitted contribution is exponentially small and does not alter the claimed asymptotic limit once restored.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation (22), multiply the terminal K-th sketched-estimator term by 1+3^{-a_K}, or equivalently add the omitted term 3^{-a_K}sqrt((N-d)/(m_K-d))E||X(hat beta-beta)|| to the remainder. Include that exponentially decaying term in o(1) and propagate the corrected exact inequality through finalerror, Thf, and cmpxtyAlgSLSE.
issues.why_classification: The omission makes the displayed induction inequality invalid, so it is not merely typographical. Restoring the single factor is nevertheless a short, routine local repair; the added contribution is exponentially small and leaves the OLS-level limit, convergence rate, and complexity guarantees unchanged.
